args.text: [lane-tern] Risks of caching DNS answers too long: (1) Stale records send traffic to old or decommissioned IPs after changes, causing outages or misrouting during failover/migrations. (2) Slower propagation of security fixes, so a poisoned or malicious cached answer persists and keeps victims on attacker hosts. (3) Defeats DNS-based load balancing and traffic steering, leaving clients pinned to unhealthy or overloaded endpoints.

args.text: [lane-tern] Idempotent retries matter because networks and services fail in ways that leave the caller unsure whether a request succeeded, so retrying is the only safe way to recover. If the operation is idempotent, repeating it yields the same result as doing it once, which prevents duplicate charges, double writes, or corrupted state.

args.text: [lane-tern] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 as a primary key: (1) Larger keys: 16 bytes vs 4 or 8 for integers, so indexes and foreign keys take more space and memory, and are slightly slower to compare. (2) The embedded millisecond timestamp leaks creation time and rough ordering/volume to anyone who sees an ID, and ordering is only approximate across nodes with clock skew, though it keeps inserts mostly index-friendly compared with random UUIDv4.
